content: Globus pharyngis, also known as lump in the throat, lump in one's throat, globus hystericus, or pharyngeal globus, refers to the persistent sensation of having phlegm or some form of obstruction in the throat, despite the absence of any actual obstruction. The characteristic lump in the throat sensation associated with globus pharyngis is typically caused by inflammation in one or more parts of the throat, such as the larynx or hypopharynx. Additionally, this sensation may be linked to anxiety disorders. The potential causes of globus pharyngis include the following, listed alphabetically: Anxiety Conversion disorder Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) Psychiatric conditions It is important to differentiate globus pharyngis from other disorders. Swallowing remains normal in individuals with this condition, meaning it is not a true case of dysphagia. However, the sensation can be quite bothersome and irritating.
